translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Honors (Enrong cidi)

Fourth year of the Hongwu reign (1371):
On the nineteenth day of the second month, the Court Examination (Palace Examination) was held.
On the twentieth day of the second month, the roll of successful candidates was called outside the Meridian Gate (Wumen), and the yellow placard of results was posted. At the Hall of Veneration of Heaven (Fengtiandian), the graduates reverently listened to the imperial proclamation; on the same day, they were appointed to their official posts and titles, and offered thanks for imperial grace at the Gate of Veneration of Heaven (Fengtianmen).
On the twenty-second day of the second month, a banquet was bestowed upon them at the Secretariat (Zhongshusheng).
On the twenty-third day of the second month, they proceeded to the Temple of the Former Teacher Confucius to perform the ritual offering of vegetables (shicai).

吳伯宗〔貫江西撫州府金谿縣，儒籍，治《書經》，字伯宗，年三十八，八月二十九日生〕。曾祖可〔宋登仕郎、漕貢進士〕；祖泰運；父儀〔元鄉貢進士〕；母何氏。具慶下。娶倪氏。鄉試第一名，會試第二十四名，授禮部員外郎。

吳公達〔貫浙江處州府麗水縣，儒籍，治《詩經》，字致中，年二十四，二月初十日生〕。曾祖艮之〔宋迪功郎〕；祖繼祖；父世德〔元鄉貢進士〕；母劉氏。具慶下。娶李氏。鄉試第二十九名，會試第一百十五名，授户部主事。

First Tier (diyi jia), 3 candidates.
Conferred the status of Metropolitan Graduate with Honors (jinshi jidi) [the first-place candidate is appointed Gentleman for Fostering Uprightness (chengzhi lang), the second-place candidate is appointed Gentleman for Managing Affairs (chengshi lang), and the third-place candidate is appointed Gentleman for Managing Affairs].

Wu Bozong 吳伯宗 [native of Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi; registered in a Confucian scholar household (ruji); specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Bozong; aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month]. His great-grandfather was Wu Ke [Court Gentleman for Ceremonial Service (dengshi lang) and Fiscal-Commission Tribute Graduate (caogong jinshi) under the Song], his grandfather was Wu Taiyun, his father is Wu Yi [Provincial Tribute Graduate (xianggong jinshi) under the Yuan], and his mother is née He. Both parents are living (juqing xia), and he is married to née Ni. He placed first in the Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination, and was appointed Vice Director (yuanwai lang) in the Ministry of Rites (libu).

Guo Chong 郭翀 [native of Huguan County, Luzhou, Shanxi; registered in a commoner household (minji); specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Zixiang; aged thirty-three]. His great-grandfather was Guo Tang, his grandfather was Guo Cheng, his father is Guo Juxian, and his mother is née Wang. Both parents are living, and he is married to née Wang. He placed eighth in the Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination, and was appointed Secretary (zhushi) in the Ministry of Personnel (libu).

Wu Gongda 吳公達 [native of Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; registered in a Confucian scholar household; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Zhizhong; aged twenty-four, born on the tenth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Wu Ganzhi [Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement (digong lang) under the Song], his grandfather was Wu Jizu, his father is Wu Shide [Provincial Tribute Graduate under the Yuan], and his mother is née Liu. Both parents are living, and he is married to née Li. He placed twenty-ninth in the Provincial Examination and one hundred fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination, and was appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue (hubu).

Yang Zili 楊自立 [registered in a Confucian household in Taihe County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi; specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); style name Ziwu 子吾; age thirty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the eighth month]. His great-grandfather was Yang Fugui 復圭 [posthumously honored in the Yuan dynasty as Grand Master forSplendid Service (Jiayi dafu), Magistrate (Yin) of Fuzhou, Light Chariot Commandant (Qingche duwei), and Earl of Hongnong Commandery (Hongnong junbo)]; his grandfather was Yang Huike 會可; his father was Yang Guan 觀; and his mother was née Guo 郭. Both parents are deceased. He is married to a woman née Guo 郭. He ranked 8th in the Provincial Examination and 3rd in the Metropolitan Examination, and was appointed Secretary (Zhushi) in the Ministry of Personnel.

Zhao Youneng 趙友能 [registered in a Confucian household in Guiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); style name Zongdian 宗典; age forty-one, born on the fifth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Zhao Chongsi 崇䄠 [Controller-general (Tongpan) of Longxing Prefecture in the Song dynasty]; his grandfather was Zhao Bikui 必奎; his father is Zhao Liangyu 良遇; and his mother is née Song 宋. Both parents are living. He is married to a woman née Liu 劉. He ranked 26th in the Provincial Examination and 73rd in the Metropolitan Examination, and was appointed Secretary (Zhushi) in the Ministry of Personnel.

Qiu Jing 仇敬 [registered in a civilian household in Quwo County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi; specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing); style name Zhongli 仲立; age thirty-two, born on the twentieth day of the sixth month]. His great-grandfather was Qiu Shouxin 守信; his grandfather was Qiu Lian 璉; his father is Qiu Weiyu 惟郁; his mother was née Du 杜; and his stepmother is née Qin 秦. Both father and stepmother are living. He is married to a woman née Yan 嚴. He ranked 1st in the Provincial Examination and 49th in the Metropolitan Examination, and was appointed Secretary (Zhushi) in the Ministry of War.

text:

勤民為務古先帝

===

謂敬天者果惟於
圜丘郊祀之際致
其精一者為敬天
歟抑他有其道歟

translation_en: …so as to draw near to the splendid customs of the ancient sovereigns and kings. Throughout the ages, imperial policy questions put to candidates in person have regularly taken revering Heaven and being diligent toward the people as their urgent priority. Among the ancient sovereigns and kings who revered Heaven and were diligent toward the people, which ones are worthy of emulation? As for what is called revering Heaven, does revering Heaven truly consist solely in exercising pure and single-minded devotion at the time of the suburban sacrifices at the Round Mound, or is there some other way to it?

title: 洪武四年進士登科錄
text:
所謂勤民者宜莫
如自朝至于日中
昃不遑暇食者矣
其所以不遑暇食
者果何為耶豈勤
===

昔而觀宜莫急於
明倫厚俗倫何由
而可明俗何由而
可厚耶三代而下

Yet why was it that he had no leisure to eat? Was he merely diligent in taking on the multitude of routine affairs? Viewed from the perspective of antiquity, nothing should be more urgent than clarifying human relationships and enriching popular customs. By what means can human relationships be clarified, and by what means can popular customs be enriched? From the Three Dynasties onward,…
